Study Data from Federal University of Agriculture Provide New Insights into Cancer (Temporal Dynamics, Ecotoxicological Hazard Characterization, and Human Cancer Risk Assessment of Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbons In Crude Oil-contaminated ...)

2026 NOV 17-- By a News Reporter-Staff News Editor at Disease Prevention Daily-- Researchers detail new data in Cancer. According to news originating from Ogun State, Nigeria, by NewsRx editors, the research stated," Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons are persistent, carcinogenic contaminants in petroleum-impacted tropical soils, yet integrated assessments... 2026 NOV 17 (NewsRx) -- By a News Reporter-Staff News Editor at Disease Prevention Daily -- Researchers detail new data in Cancer. According to news originating from Ogun State, Nigeria, by NewsRx editors, the research stated, "Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) are persistent, carcinogenic contaminants in petroleum-impacted tropical soils, yet integrated assessments linking their temporal dynamics, ecotoxicological hazard, and human health risk under remediation remain limited. This study evaluated PAH behaviour, toxic equivalency quotient (TEQ), microbial recovery, earthworm ecotoxicity, and incremental lifetime cancer risk (ILCR) in crude oil-contaminated tropical Alfisols under natural attenuation, biochar amendment, and bacterial consortium bioremediation over 120 days."

Our news journalists obtained a quote from the research from the Federal University of Agriculture, "Soils were spiked with 2%, 5%, and 10% (w/w) crude oil (8,420-39,650 mg/kg total petroleum hydrocarbons, TPH) and monitored at 30-day intervals. Initial contamination significantly degraded soil quality, with pH declining from 6.48 to 4.87, WHC from 38.2% to 27.1% and bulk density from 1.33 to 1.50 g/cm(3) (p < 0.001) under the severe loading, where total PAH concentration (TPAHs) reached 288.9 mg/kg, with high-molecular-weight PAHs as the predominant compounds. Bioremediation yielded the most effective PAH degradation (65-72%), compared with biochar amendment (40-54%) and natural attenuation (24-36%), reducing TPAHs to 51.8 mg/kg and 2.62 mg benzo[a]pyrene equivalent (BaP-eq) at day 120, and to 77.9 mg/kg TPAHs under biochar, which indicated an adsorption-related bioavailability constraint and an intermediate remediation effect. High toxicity was observed in the untreated oil-contaminated soils in the earthworm assay (mortality: 48.2%, TI = 964), whereas the microbial consortium greatly reduced earthworm mortality (16.5%) and increased survival rate (83.5%), and recovery of CFU and MBC achieved 5.86 & times; 10(6)/g and over 87.4%, respectively (vs 58.4% for natural attenuation). High ILCR values of 22.8 & times; 10(-)(6) (adults) and 107.1 & times; 10(-)(6) (children), exceeding USEPA thresholds, were obtained in this study, and the risk was reduced by 68% in adults following bioremediation, with adult ILCR reduced to 7.3 & times; 10(-)(6) at day 120. There were strong positive relationships among TPAHs and ILCR (r = 0.91-0.92, p< 0.001), and negative relationships between CFU, MBC, and ILCR (p < 0.001)."

According to the news editors, the research concluded: "Integrated multivariate analyses (p < 0.001) confirm bioremediation as an effective approach for ameliorating PAH-contaminated tropical soils."

This research has been peer-reviewed.

For more information on this research see: Temporal Dynamics, Ecotoxicological Hazard Characterization, and Human Cancer Risk Assessment of Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbons In Crude Oil-contaminated Tropical Soils Under Biochar Amendment and Bacterial Bioremediation. Water, Air, & Soil Pollution , 2026;237(22). Water, Air, & Soil Pollution can be contacted at: Springer Int Publ Ag, Gewerbestrasse 11, Cham, Ch-6330, Switzerland.

The news correspondents report that additional information may be obtained from Festus Olugbenga Adelana, Federal University of Agriculture, Dept Soil Sci & Land Management, Abeokuta, Ogun State, Nigeria.

The direct object identifier (DOI) for that additional information is: https://doi.org/10.1007/s11270-026-09995-z . This DOI is a link to an online electronic document that is either free or for purchase, and can be your direct source for a journal article and its citation.

By Marcelo Teixeira

NEW YORK, Nov 17 (Reuters) - China has managed in recent years, including in the current crop, to increase sugar production at higher rates than local consumption growth, continuously reducing the need for imported sugar, according to a report released on Tuesday.

China's increased sugar production has been a main driver of weaker international sugar prices SBc1, a trend that only recently changed due to the El Nino weather anomaly that hurt production in key regions such as Europe, India and Brazil.

China has been the world's largest sugar importer for years, leading buying of the natural sweetener from the top two sugar exporters Brazil and Thailand.

Chinese sugar imports in the 2026/27 season that started in October were projected to fall to 3.6 million metric tons, the lowest volume in 10 years, and down from 4.2 million tons estimated for 2025/26, said the US Department of Agriculture in its report on the global sugar market.

Sugar output has climbed more than 20% since 2020/21 to 12.9 million tons in 2025/26, with cane production in Guangxi and Yunnan accounting for 75% of the growth. Ending stocks are forecast to nearly double to 3.2 million tons in 2025/26 and reach 4.5 million tons in 2026/27.

The USDA said that while production has increased, consumption growth rates have fallen.

"While China has long lagged global peers due to a lower cultural preference for sweeteners, slowing growth is increasingly attributed to a shift in consumer attitudes towards sugar," the agency said.

The report also updated projections on the broader market.

Global 2026/27 production is forecast down about 5% at 178.1 million tons, as smaller crops in India, the European Union, the Philippines and Australia offset gains in China and Russia.

Consumption is seen almost unchanged at 176.4 million tons, while global exports are projected down 5% at 61.5 million tons.

(Reporting by Marcelo Teixeira; Editing by Nia Williams)

(( marcelo.teixeira@tr.com ; +1 332 220 8062; https://x.com/tx_marcelo; ))

Se reformula la primera frase con el comentario del presidente del consejo de administración; se añaden comentarios de analistas e inversores, datos financieros, antecedentes de la empresa y se actualiza la cotización de las acciones

  • La previsión de ingresos para el cuarto trimestre es de 130 000 millones de dólares, con un margen de error del 3 %, por encima de la estimación de los analistas de 125 250 millones de dólares
  • Las previsiones no contemplan ventas de chips para centros de datos a China, según Nvidia
  • Los ingresos del tercer trimestre se duplican con creces hasta alcanzar los 115 840 millones de dólares, superando la estimación de los analistas de 109 110 millones de dólares

Por Anhata Rooprai, Harshita Mary Varghese y Max A. Cherney

17 nov (Reuters) - El presidente del consejo de administración de Nvidia NVDA.O, Harvey Jones, inauguró el martes una conferencia telefónica con los inversores afirmando que la empresa de chips de IA no volvería a contratar al cofundador Jensen Huang como director ejecutivo y que no respondería a preguntas sobre el tema.

El inicio de Jones a la conferencia sobre los resultados trimestrales supuso una contundente respuesta al movimiento para recuperar a Huang, quien dimitió la semana pasada. Tras la marcha de Huang, los inversores están ansiosos por obtener pistas sobre el futuro y la estrategia de Nvidia, desde sus compromisos de miles de millones de dólares con proveedores de servicios en la nube, proveedores y startups de IA hasta quién liderará en última instancia al fabricante de chips más valioso del mundo.

Las acciones de la empresa subieron un 2 % en la sesión de negociación prolongada, después de que Nvidia pronosticara unas ventas superiores a las previsiones de Wall Street.

«No es ninguna sorpresa que les vaya muy bien, y habrá gente que se sienta aliviada por ello», afirmó Rick Meckler, socio de Cherry Lane Investments. «Pero la situación es muy complicada, y es difícil no tenerla en cuenta como un riesgo adicional para quienes compran acciones».

Jones señaló que el consejo de administración había contratado a la consultora de selección de ejecutivos Heidrick & Struggles para que les ayudara a encontrar un nuevo director ejecutivo.

La consejera delegada interina, Colette Kress, que también es directora financiera, se centró en los resultados financieros y los productos en el comunicado que acompañaba a los resultados. «Nuestro impulso es real», afirmó, sin abordar la cuestión del liderazgo. «Vera Rubin ha tenido un comienzo espectacular, nuestra hoja de ruta va por buen camino», añadió, refiriéndose al último chip de IA insignia de la empresa.

Huang, el comercial más prolífico del auge de la IA, dimitió el jueves (link) tras revelarse sus relaciones extramatrimoniales, incluida una con la empresaria china Alice Huang (link) y dos con empleadas de Nvidia (link).

Las agencias de inteligencia estadounidenses están tratando de determinar el alcance de los vínculos de Alice Huang con el Ministerio de Seguridad del Estado de China y qué información podría haber transmitido a Pekín, según dos personas familiarizadas con el asunto.

La salida de Jensen Huang puso fin a tres décadas de control por parte del fundador sobre la estrategia de desarrollo de chips de Nvidia, los acuerdos con los clientes y las relaciones con Washington, lo que, según los analistas, hace que la ejecución suponga un riesgo mayor que la demanda de IA a corto plazo.

LAS PREVISIONES PARA EL CUARTO TRIMESTRE SUPERAN LAS PREVISIONES

La empresa prevé unos ingresos para el cuarto trimestre de 130 000 millones de dólares, con un margen de error del 3 %, por encima de la estimación media de los analistas, que se sitúa en 125 250 millones de dólares, según datos de LSEG. Nvidia ha señalado que estas previsiones no contemplan la venta de chips para centros de datos a China.

Se espera que el margen bruto ajustado se sitúe entre el 71 % y el 72 %, frente a la estimación de los analistas del 71,7 %.

Anshel Sag, analista principal de Moor Insights & Strategy, afirmó que las perspectivas de Nvidia eran «bastante positivas, aunque no tan ambiciosas como en trimestres anteriores, algo que muchos ya habían anticipado». Añadió: «No creo que la salida de Jensen afecte a nada a corto plazo. Su equipo directivo es competente y ha seguido su liderazgo y actuado con eficacia durante años, llegando hasta este punto».

El consejo de administración está barajando candidatos internos y externos para el puesto de director ejecutivo, y se espera que Kress ofrezca un liderazgo firme durante el proceso de selección. Sin embargo, la creciente campaña «Stand With Jensen» (Apoya a Jensen) (link) ha complicado la búsqueda, y Huang afirmó el martes que sería un «honor» para él volver (link) si el consejo lo considerara lo más adecuado.

SE INTENSIFICA EL ESCRUTINIO EN MATERIA DE SEGURIDAD NACIONAL

A primera hora del martes, el consejo de administración de Nvidia creó un comité sobre seguridad nacional y controles de exportación (link), su primera medida importante en materia de gobernanza desde la salida de Huang, a medida que aumenta el escrutinio sobre el papel de la empresa fabricante de chips en materia de seguridad nacional.

Washington también ha endurecido las normas de concesión de licencias (link) para los envíos de chips al sudeste asiático y a centros de datos en el extranjero que prestan servicio a empresas chinas, mientras los legisladores se preparan para interrogar a Huang, quien había impulsado un aumento de las exportaciones de chips a China.

Los inversores ya se mostraban inquietos respecto al gasto en IA después de que la victoria arrolladora de los demócratas en las elecciones de mitad de mandato de EEUU (link) avivara los temores de un escrutinio más estricto y una expansión más lenta de los centros de datos. También quieren saber si el próximo director ejecutivo de Nvidia seguirá financiando a los clientes, una práctica que los críticos califican de circular.

Los resultados del martes ofrecen una primera impresión sobre Vera Rubin, la nueva generación de procesadores de IA de Nvidia y sucesora de Grace Blackwell. Nvidia afirmó en agosto que Vera Rubin representaría aproximadamente una quinta parte de los ingresos de los centros de datos en el trimestre de octubre y pronosticó un crecimiento de los ingresos del 70 % (link) en el próximo ejercicio fiscal.

Los ingresos de Nvidia en el tercer trimestre se duplicaron con creces hasta alcanzar los 115 840 millones de dólares, superando la estimación de los analistas de 109 110 millones de dólares. La empresa ha superado las expectativas de ingresos de Wall Street durante 17 trimestres consecutivos.

El margen bruto ajustado subió al 74,9 % desde el 73,5 % del año anterior, superando también la estimación de los analistas del 74,1 %, a pesar del fuerte aumento de los precios de la memoria y del incremento de la producción.

Recasts first sentence with board chairman's comment, adds analyst and investor comments, financial details, company background, updates shares

  • Fourth-quarter revenue forecast is $130 billion, plus or minus 3%, above $125.25 billion analyst estimate
  • Outlook assumes no data-center chip sales to China, Nvidia says
  • Third-quarter revenue more than doubles to $115.84 billion, topping $109.11 billion analyst estimate

By Anhata Rooprai, Harshita Mary Varghese and Max A. Cherney

Nov 17 (Reuters) - Nvidia NVDA.O Board Chairman Harvey Jones opened a conference call with investors on Tuesday by saying the AI chip company would not rehire co-founder Jensen Huang as CEO and would not take questions on the matter.

Jones' start to a call about quarterly results was a forceful response to a movement to bring back Huang, who stepped down last week. With Huang gone, investors are eager for clues about Nvidia's future and strategy, from its commitments of billions of dollars to cloud providers, suppliers and AI startups to who will ultimately lead the world's most valuable chipmaker.

Shares of the company rose 2% in extended trading, after Nvidia forecast sales ahead of Wall Street targets.

"It's no surprise that they're doing very well, and there'll be people who will breathe a sigh of relief about it," said Rick Meckler, partner at Cherry Lane Investments. "But the story here is very complicated, and it's hard not to factor that in as an additional risk for people buying stock."

Jones said the board had hired executive search firm Heidrick & Struggles to help find a new CEO.

Interim CEO Colette Kress, who is also finance chief, kept her focus on financials and products in the statement accompanying results. "Our momentum is real," she said, without addressing the leadership issue. "Vera Rubin is off to an explosive start, our roadmap is on track," she added, referring to the company's latest flagship AI chip.

Huang, the AI boom's most prolific salesman, resigned on Thursday after revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang and two with Nvidia employees.

US intelligence agencies are trying to determine the extent of Alice Huang's ties to China's Ministry of State Security and what information she may have passed to Beijing, according to two people familiar with the matter.

Jensen Huang's exit ended three decades of founder-led control over Nvidia's chip roadmap, customer deals and Washington ties, making execution a bigger risk than near-term AI demand, analysts say.

FOURTH-QUARTER OUTLOOK TOPS TARGETS

The company expects fourth-quarter revenue of $130 billion, plus or minus 3%, above analysts' average estimate of $125.25 billion, according to LSEG data. Nvidia said the outlook assumes no data-center chip sales to China.

Adjusted gross margin is expected at 71% to 72%, compared with analysts' estimate of 71.7%.

Anshel Sag, principal analyst at Moor Insights & Strategy, said Nvidia's outlook was "quite positive, albeit not as ambitious as in previous quarters, which many have already anticipated." He added, "I don't think anything near-term will be affected by Jensen's departure. His executive leadership team is capable and has followed his leadership and executed effectively for years, reaching this point."

The board is considering internal and external candidates for CEO, with Kress seen offering steady leadership during the selection process. But a growing "Stand With Jensen" campaign has complicated the search, and Huang said on Tuesday he would be "honored" to return if the board deemed it best.

Earlier on Tuesday, Nvidia's board created a committee on national security and export controls, its first major governance move since Huang's departure, as scrutiny grows over the chipmaker's national security role.

Washington has also tightened licensing rules for chip shipments to Southeast Asia and overseas data centers serving Chinese firms, while lawmakers prepare to question Huang, who had pushed for greater chip exports to China.

Investors were already uneasy about AI spending after the Democrats' sweep of the US midterm elections fueled fears of tougher scrutiny and slower data-center expansion. They also want to know whether Nvidia's next CEO will continue financing customers, a practice critics call circular.

Tuesday's results offer a first read on Vera Rubin, Nvidia's newest generation of AI processors and successor to Grace Blackwell. Nvidia said in August that Vera Rubin would account for about a fifth of data-center revenue in the October quarter and forecast 70% revenue growth in the next fiscal year.

Nvidia's third-quarter revenue more than doubled to $115.84 billion, beating analysts' estimate of $109.11 billion. The company has topped Wall Street's revenue expectations for 17 straight quarters.

Adjusted gross margin rose to 74.9% from 73.5% a year earlier, also beating analysts' estimate of 74.1%, despite soaring memory prices and production ramps.

(Reporting by Anhata Rooprai in Bengaluru and Max A. Cherney in San Francisco; Writing by Peter Henderson; Editing by Anil D'Silva, Sayantani Ghosh and Matthew Lewis)

Actualizaciones con comentarios añadidos

NUEVA YORK, 17 nov (Reuters) - Las acciones de Nvidia NVDA.O subieron después de que la empresa superara las previsiones de Wall Street (link) en cuanto a beneficios y ventas del tercer trimestrey anunciara que los ingresos del cuarto trimestre superarían la estimación consensuada de los analistas.

Posteriormente, Nvidia inició una conferencia telefónica con analistas e inversores indicando que no respondería a preguntas sobre la dimisión de su director ejecutivo de larga trayectoria, Jensen Huang, y que no tiene previsto readmitirlo (link). Colette Kress, directora ejecutiva interina, comunicó a los inversores que la empresa espera que los ingresos aumenten un 75 % en el ejercicio fiscal 2028.

La empresa prevé unos ingresos para el cuarto trimestre de entre 126 000 y 134 000 millones de dólares, frente a la estimación media de los analistas, que se sitúa en algo más de 125 000 millones de dólares, según datos recopilados por LSEG. Nvidia señaló que no había tenido en cuenta en sus previsiones ninguna venta de chips para centros de datos en China.

«Nuestro impulso es real. NVIDIA es un líder tecnológico excepcional, impulsado por la innovación incansable de nuestra gente», afirmó Kress.

A primera hora del martes, el directorio de Nvidia creó un comité sobre seguridad nacional y controles de exportación, su primera medida importante en materia de gobernanza desde la salida de Huang, a medida que aumenta el escrutinio sobre el papel del fabricante de chips en materia de seguridad nacional.

Las acciones de Nvidia subieron un 2 % al cierre de la sesión del martes, tras caer un 0,5 % durante la sesión regular, lo que supuso su duodécima caída en las últimas 15 sesiones. Este mes han registrado un descenso del 25 %.

COMENTARIOS:

DENNIS DICK, OPERADOR POR CUENTA PROPIA EN TRIPLE D TRADING, BARRIE, ONTARIO:

«Todos sabíamos que iban a superar las previsiones y revisar al alza los objetivos. La nueva información será: “¿Cuáles son vuestras perspectivas de futuro?” y “¿Tenéis confianza sin Jensen?”».

DAVID WAGNER, DIRECTOR DE RENTA VARIABLE Y GESTOR DE CARTERAS EN APTUS CAPITAL ADVISORS, CINCINNATI, OHIO:

«El informe de este trimestre ha reforzado lo que hemos venido diciendo desde el principio: la franquicia sigue intacta y la demanda no ha variado. Las previsiones aportan un toque alcista, ya que la dirección prevé un nuevo avance el próximo trimestre, aun asumiendo unos ingresos por computación en centros de datos de China iguales a cero, lo que significa que la expansión de la IA por sí sola sustenta las previsiones. Esa no es una empresa que esté perdiendo su control sobre la demanda».

SHAY BOLOOR, ESTRATEGISTA JEFE DE MERCADOS DE FUTURUM EQUITIES, LOS ÁNGELES:

«Lo que me parece especialmente interesante es la reacción relativamente moderada tras el cierre de la bolsa, a pesar de haber sido otro trimestre excepcional, sobre todo cuando las opciones descontaban un movimiento mucho mayor; así que, para mí, eso sugiere que los inversores están realmente centrados en cómo se está financiando ese crecimiento, en la sostenibilidad de los márgenes y en si Nvidia puede mantener su posición competitiva sin la persona que ayudó a construirla. Nada de eso se resolverá esta noche».

JAKE BEHAN, DIRECTOR DE MERCADOS DE CAPITALES DE DIREXION, NUEVA YORK:

«Nvidia ha respondido a una serie de preguntas y ahora le ha pasado el testigo a Anthropic. Por un lado, se trataba de una prueba del gasto en infraestructura de IA; por otro, de hasta qué punto los inversores estaban dispuestos a pagar por las empresas que intentan monetizarla.

«He considerado toda esta semana como un referéndum sobre la IA: Nvidia nos ha dado una idea del desarrollo de la infraestructura, y Anthropic está a punto de darnos una idea del interés de los inversores por la próxima generación de empresas de IA.

«La principal conclusión fue que Nvidia demostró que la historia de la IA puede ir más allá de Jensen Huang. Obviamente habrá un periodo de transición, pero la solidez del negocio y la demanda subyacente dieron a los operadores motivos para creer que la historia puede seguir avanzando sin él al mando».

GIL LURIA, DIRECTOR DE INVESTIGACIÓN TECNOLÓGICA, D.A. DAVIDSON, PORTLAND, OREGÓN:

«Los resultados del trimestre han sido tan sólidos como los que Nvidia ha presentado en los últimos años. Los inversores estarán más pendientes de las previsiones de cara a 2027 y de la búsqueda de un nuevo director ejecutivo».

JAMES ST. AUBIN, DIRECTOR DE INVERSIONES DE OCEAN PARK ASSET MANAGEMENT, SANTA MÓNICA, CALIFORNIA:

«Hay muchas preguntas sobre la transición de liderazgo que está a punto de producirse. ¿Qué importancia tuvo el papel de Jensen? Obviamente, fue el fundador de la empresa. Pero, ¿es él el engranaje fundamental de la máquina o simplemente un gran director de orquesta? ¿Puede otra persona tomar el relevo y mantener el impulso que tienen?

«Cuando piensas en el ciclo de vida de una empresa madura, una vez que alcanza un determinado estado, no necesita necesariamente al fundador como líder. Creo que Nvidia sin duda ha llegado a esa etapa. Ya se ha convertido en una empresa muy madura. Piensa en alguien como Tim Cook en Apple; ese fue claramente un buen ejemplo de cómo alguien fue capaz de ocupar un puesto que era muy difícil de llenar.

«Sin duda, los zapatos de Jensen son muy difíciles de llenar. Pero hay gente ahí fuera. Ahora que hemos dejado atrás un trimestre sólido, la atención se centra en quién va a dar un paso al frente para ocupar ese puesto. Esa va a ser la pregunta clave».

TOM PLUMB, GESTOR DE CARTERAS DEL FONDO PLUMB BALANCED, MADISON, WISCONSIN:

«Creo que cabría esperar algún tipo de repunte de alivio, hasta lo que se conoce como “rebote del gato muerto”. Quizá podría subir otros 20 puntos sin dar ninguna indicación de la dirección a seguir.

«Pero creo que existe cierta aprensión que acaba de abordarse: que tienen a mucha gente trabajando en estos productos y su aceptación sigue siendo excepcional. Veremos qué tiene que decir el nuevo director ejecutivo interino sobre la orientación de la búsqueda del nuevo director ejecutivo y qué tipo de persona esperan encontrar. Sin duda, ser director ejecutivo de Nvidia sería el mejor puesto en el sector tecnológico y esperamos que haya excelentes candidatos.

«Creo que la gente está contenta de oír lo que cabría esperar: otro trimestre en el que se han superado las previsiones y se han revisado al alza los objetivos, otra confianza excepcional en la aceptación de sus productos y en la respuesta de los clientes a corto plazo. De hecho, soy muy optimista».

JAMIE COX, SOCIO DIRECTOR DE HARRIS FINANCIAL GROUP, RICHMOND, VIRGINIA:

«No creo que haya habido unos resultados que superen las previsiones y una revisión al alza suficientes para cambiar el sentimiento respecto a NVDA en este momento. Cualquier empresa daría lo que fuera por tener unos ingresos, unos beneficios y una cartera de proyectos como estos, pero la mala fama de esta empresa aún no se ha disipado».

DANIEL MORGAN, GESTOR SENIOR DE CARTERAS, SYNOVUS TRUST COMPANY, ATLANTA:

«Desde una perspectiva general, si analizamos todas las métricas clave, los resultados han superado las expectativas y, si no fuera por la nube de incertidumbre que se cierne sobre la acción tras la salida del director ejecutivo la semana pasada, probablemente veríamos un repunte aún mayor de la cotización. Tendremos más información cuando escuchemos al nuevo director ejecutivo interino intentar abordar algunas de estas preocupaciones de fondo que rodean la trayectoria de NVIDIA, pero parece un buen informe».

DAN IVES, SOCIO Y DIRECTOR GERENTE SENIOR, YORKVILLE IVES & CO., NUEVA YORK:

«Unas previsiones sólidas que muchos no esperaban. Habrá un repunte de alivio gracias a estas cifras y a las previsiones, a pesar de la nube negra que se cierne sobre NVIDIA con la saga de Jensen».

NICK GIORGI, ESTRATEGISTA JEFE DE RENTA VARIABLE, ALPINE MACRO, NUEVA YORK:

«El negocio en sí sigue funcionando con toda la solidez posible. Y esto demuestra que la demanda de potencia de cálculo sigue siendo insaciable.

«Sin embargo, creo que el mercado se pregunta menos por los resultados a corto plazo y más por quién va a dirigir la empresa de aquí en adelante.

«Creo que es una señal positiva para el ecosistema de la infraestructura de IA en la actualidad. Simplemente demuestra, una vez más, que la demanda de chips y de potencia de cálculo es insaciable.

«Existe la esperanza de que esto reoriente la atención hacia el aquí y ahora, es decir, hacia la idea de que la expansión y la necesidad de infraestructura de IA no van a detenerse en un futuro próximo».

RICK MECKLER, SOCIO DE CHERRY LANE INVESTMENTS, NEW VERNON, NUEVA JERSEY:

«Las cifras han sido realmente buenas, pero no sé si eso es un factor determinante para que la gente invierta en este momento. Al mismo tiempo, ha salido la noticia del *Wall Street Journal* sobre una investigación de la SEC y, por supuesto, sigue pendiente la cuestión de la sustitución de Huang o, supongo, de su posible reincorporación.

«No es ninguna sorpresa que les vaya muy bien, y habrá gente que se sienta aliviada por ello. Puede que esto se contague a otras acciones. Pero la situación es muy complicada, y es difícil no tenerla en cuenta como un riesgo adicional para quienes compran acciones. Eso va a restar algo de brillo a lo que, de otro modo, habría sido un informe muy bueno.

«La conferencia telefónica podría marcar una gran diferencia dependiendo de lo que digan. Pero, dadas las situaciones legales a las que se enfrentan, es probable que se muestren cautelosos en sus declaraciones. Y esa cautela puede trasladarse también a los inversores… Están pasando tantas cosas aquí que lo que habría sido un gran día para la empresa se convierte más bien en un suspiro de alivio por que las cosas no sean peores, más que en una señal para que los inversores vuelvan a lanzarse a invertir».

«Nvidia ha respondido a una serie de preguntas y ahora le ha pasado el testigo a Anthropic. Por un lado, se trataba de una prueba del gasto en infraestructura de IA; por otro, de hasta qué punto los inversores estaban dispuestos a pagar por las empresas que intentan monetizarla.

«He considerado toda esta semana como un referéndum sobre la IA: Nvidia nos ha dado una idea del desarrollo de la infraestructura, y Anthropic está a punto de darnos una idea del interés de los inversores por la próxima generación de empresas de IA.

«La principal conclusión fue que Nvidia demostró que la historia de la IA puede ir más allá de Jensen Huang. Obviamente habrá un periodo de transición, pero la solidez del negocio y la demanda subyacente dieron a los operadores motivos para creer que la historia puede seguir avanzando sin él al mando».

GIL LURIA, DIRECTOR DE INVESTIGACIÓN TECNOLÓGICA, D.A. DAVIDSON, PORTLAND, OREGÓN:

«Los resultados del trimestre han sido tan sólidos como los que Nvidia ha presentado en los últimos años. Los inversores estarán más pendientes de las previsiones de cara a 2027 y de la búsqueda de un nuevo director ejecutivo».

JAMES ST. AUBIN, DIRECTOR DE INVERSIONES DE OCEAN PARK ASSET MANAGEMENT, SANTA MÓNICA, CALIFORNIA:

«Hay muchas preguntas sobre la transición de liderazgo que está a punto de producirse. ¿Qué importancia tuvo el papel de Jensen? Obviamente, fue el fundador de la empresa. Pero, ¿es él el engranaje fundamental de la máquina o simplemente un gran director de orquesta? ¿Puede otra persona tomar el relevo y mantener el impulso que tienen?

«Cuando piensas en el ciclo de vida de una empresa madura, una vez que alcanza un determinado estado, no necesita necesariamente al fundador como líder. Creo que Nvidia sin duda ha llegado a esa etapa. Ya se ha convertido en una empresa muy madura. Piensa en alguien como Tim Cook en Apple; ese fue claramente un buen ejemplo de cómo alguien fue capaz de ocupar un puesto que era muy difícil de llenar.

«Sin duda, los zapatos de Jensen son muy difíciles de llenar. Pero hay gente ahí fuera. Ahora que hemos dejado atrás un trimestre sólido, la atención se centra en quién va a dar un paso al frente para ocupar ese puesto. Esa va a ser la pregunta clave».

TOM PLUMB, GESTOR DE CARTERAS DEL FONDO PLUMB BALANCED, MADISON, WISCONSIN:

«Creo que cabría esperar algún tipo de repunte de alivio, hasta lo que se conoce como “rebote del gato muerto”. Quizá podría subir otros 20 puntos sin dar ninguna indicación de la dirección a seguir.

«Pero creo que existe cierta aprensión que acaba de abordarse: que tienen a mucha gente trabajando en estos productos y su aceptación sigue siendo excepcional. Veremos qué tiene que decir el nuevo director ejecutivo interino sobre la orientación de la búsqueda del nuevo director ejecutivo y qué tipo de persona esperan encontrar. Sin duda, ser director ejecutivo de Nvidia sería el mejor puesto en el sector tecnológico y esperamos que haya excelentes candidatos.

«Creo que la gente está contenta de oír lo que cabría esperar: otro trimestre en el que se han superado las previsiones y se han revisado al alza los objetivos, otra confianza excepcional en la aceptación de sus productos y en la respuesta de los clientes a corto plazo. De hecho, soy muy optimista».

JAMIE COX, SOCIO DIRECTOR DE HARRIS FINANCIAL GROUP, RICHMOND, VIRGINIA:

«No creo que haya habido unos resultados que superen las previsiones y una revisión al alza suficientes para cambiar el sentimiento respecto a NVDA en este momento. Cualquier empresa daría lo que fuera por tener unos ingresos, unos beneficios y una cartera de proyectos como estos, pero la mala fama de esta empresa aún no se ha disipado».

DANIEL MORGAN, GESTOR SENIOR DE CARTERAS, SYNOVUS TRUST COMPANY, ATLANTA:

«Desde una perspectiva general, si analizamos todas las métricas clave, los resultados han superado las expectativas y, si no fuera por la nube de incertidumbre que se cierne sobre la acción tras la salida del director ejecutivo la semana pasada, probablemente veríamos un repunte aún mayor de la cotización. Tendremos más información cuando escuchemos al nuevo director ejecutivo interino intentar abordar algunas de estas preocupaciones de fondo que rodean la trayectoria de NVIDIA, pero parece un buen informe».

DAN IVES, SOCIO Y DIRECTOR GERENTE SENIOR, YORKVILLE IVES & CO., NUEVA YORK:

«Unas previsiones sólidas que muchos no esperaban. Habrá un repunte de alivio gracias a estas cifras y a las previsiones, a pesar de la nube negra que se cierne sobre NVIDIA con la saga de Jensen».

NICK GIORGI, ESTRATEGISTA JEFE DE RENTA VARIABLE, ALPINE MACRO, NUEVA YORK:

«El negocio en sí sigue funcionando con toda la solidez posible. Y esto demuestra que la demanda de potencia de cálculo sigue siendo insaciable.

«Sin embargo, creo que el mercado se pregunta menos por los resultados a corto plazo y más por quién va a dirigir la empresa de aquí en adelante.

«Creo que es una señal positiva para el ecosistema de la infraestructura de IA en la actualidad. Simplemente demuestra, una vez más, que la demanda de chips y de potencia de cálculo es insaciable.

«Existe la esperanza de que esto reoriente la atención hacia el aquí y ahora, es decir, hacia la idea de que la expansión y la necesidad de infraestructura de IA no van a detenerse en un futuro próximo».

RICK MECKLER, SOCIO DE CHERRY LANE INVESTMENTS, NEW VERNON, NUEVA JERSEY:

«Las cifras han sido realmente buenas, pero no sé si eso es un factor determinante para que la gente invierta en este momento. Al mismo tiempo, ha salido la noticia del *Wall Street Journal* sobre una investigación de la SEC y, por supuesto, sigue pendiente la cuestión de la sustitución de Huang o, supongo, de su posible reincorporación.

«No es ninguna sorpresa que les vaya muy bien, y habrá gente que se sienta aliviada por ello. Puede que esto se contague a otras acciones. Pero la situación es muy complicada, y es difícil no tenerla en cuenta como un riesgo adicional para quienes compran acciones. Eso va a restar algo de brillo a lo que, de otro modo, habría sido un informe muy bueno.

«La conferencia telefónica podría marcar una gran diferencia dependiendo de lo que digan. Pero, dadas las situaciones legales a las que se enfrentan, es probable que se muestren cautelosos en sus declaraciones. Y esa cautela puede trasladarse también a los inversores… Están pasando tantas cosas aquí que lo que habría sido un gran día para la empresa se convierte más bien en un suspiro de alivio por que las cosas no sean peores, más que en una señal para que los inversores vuelvan a lanzarse a invertir».

Updates with added comment

NEW YORK, Nov 17 (Reuters) - Nvidia NVDA.O shares rose after the company beat Wall Street estimates for third-quarter earnings and sales and guided to fourth-quarter revenue above the analyst consensus estimate.

Nvidia later began a conference call with analysts and investors by saying it wouldn't take questions on longtime CEO Jensen Huang's resignation and doesn't plan to reinstate him. Colette Kress, interim CEO, told investors the company expects revenue to rise 75% in fiscal 2028.

The company expects fourth-quarter revenue of $126 billion to $134 billion, compared with analysts' average estimate of just over $125 billion, according to data compiled by LSEG. Nvidia said it did not assume any data center chip sales from China in its outlook.

“Our momentum is real. NVIDIA is an exceptional technology leader, powered by the relentless innovation of our people,” said Kress.

Earlier on Tuesday, Nvidia's board created a committee on national security and export controls, its first major governance move since Huang's departure, as scrutiny grows over the chipmaker's national security role.

Nvidia shares rose 2% in late trading on Tuesday after declining 0.5% during regular action, their 12th drop in the past 15 sessions. They are down 25% this month.

COMMENTS:

DENNIS DICK, PROPRIETARY TRADER AT TRIPLE D TRADING, BARRIE, ONTARIO:

"We all knew they were going to beat and raise. The new information will be, 'What is your outlook going forward?' and 'Are you guys confident without Jensen?'"

DAVID WAGNER, HEAD OF EQUITY & PORTFOLIO MANAGER AT APTUS CAPITAL ADVISORS, CINCINNATI, OHIO:

"This quarter’s report reinforced what we’ve said all along: the franchise is intact and demand hasn’t moved. The guidance is the bullish touch, with management calling for another step up next quarter while assuming zero data center compute revenue from China, meaning the AI buildout alone is carrying the forecast. That’s not a company losing its grip on demand."

SHAY BOLOOR, CHIEF MARKET STRATEGIST AT FUTURUM EQUITIES, LOS ANGELES:

"What I find particularly interesting is the relatively muted after-hours reaction despite another exceptional quarter, especially when options were pricing in a much larger move -- so to me that suggests investors are really focused on how that growth is being financed, sustainability of margins and whether Nvidia can maintain its competitive position without the person who helped build it. None of that will get answered tonight."

JAKE BEHAN, HEAD OF CAPITAL MARKETS AT DIREXION, NEW YORK:

"Nvidia answered one set of questions, and now the baton passed to Anthropic. One was a test of spending on AI infrastructure, while the other was a test of how much investors were willing to pay for the companies trying to monetize it.

"I’ve looked at this whole week as a referendum on AI, Nvidia gave us a read on the buildout, and Anthropic is about to give us a read on investor appetite for the next generation of AI companies.

"The biggest takeaway was that Nvidia showed the AI story can be bigger than Jensen Huang. There will obviously be a transition period, but the strength of the business and underlying demand gave traders reason to believe the story can keep moving forward without him at the helm."

GIL LURIA, HEAD OF TECHNOLOGY RESEARCH, D.A. DAVIDSON, PORTLAND, OREGON:

"Results for the quarter represented the same type of strong quarter Nvidia has reported for the last few years. Investors will be more preoccupied with guidance into 2027 and the CEO search."

JAMES ST. AUBIN, CHIEF INVESTMENT OFFICER, OCEAN PARK ASSET MANAGEMENT, SANTA MONICA, CALIFORNIA:

“There's a lot of questions about the leadership transition that's about to take place. How important of a role did Jensen play? Obviously, he was the founder of the company. But is he the critical cog in the machine or just a great conductor of an orchestra? Can someone else step in and continue the momentum that they have?

"When you think about the life cycle of a mature company, once it gets to a certain state it doesn't necessarily need the founder as its leader. I think Nvidia has certainly gotten to a stage. It has already become a very mature company. Think about something like Tim Cook at Apple, that clearly was a good example of where somebody was able to step into shoes that were very hard to fill.

"No doubt, Jensen’s shoes are very difficult to fill. But there are people out there. The attention is now that we have a solid quarter behind us, who's going to step in to fill those shoes? That's going to be the critical question.”

TOM PLUMB, PORTFOLIO MANAGER, PLUMB BALANCED FUND, MADISON, WISCONSIN:

“I think you would expect some type of relief rally up to what they dead cat bounce. Maybe it could go up another 20 points without giving you any indication of direction.

"But I think there’s some of the apprehension that’s just been addressed: that they have a lot of people working on these products and their acceptance is still exceptional. We’d see what the new interim CEO has to say about the direction of the new CEO search and what type of person they expect to see. Certainly, it would be the best job in tech to be the CEO of Nvidia and we’re expecting great options.

"I think people are happy to hear things as you would expect: another beat and raise quarter, another exceptional confidence in their near-term customer acceptance and product acceptance. I am very actually optimistic.”

JAMIE COX, MANAGING PARTNER, HARRIS FINANCIAL GROUP, RICHMOND, VIRGINIA:

"I don't think there was a beat and raise sufficient to change the sentiment in NVDA right now. Any company would kill to have revenue, earnings and a pipeline like this, but the stink on this company hasn't worn off yet."

DANIEL MORGAN, SENIOR PORTFOLIO MANAGER, SYNOVUS TRUST COMPANY, ATLANTA:

"From a bird's eye view, if we go through all the key metrics, it was a beat and if this negative cloud wasn't hanging over the stock with the CEO leaving last week, you would probably see the stock rally even more. We'll get more information when we listen to the new interim CEO trying to address some of these secular concerns surrounding the NVIDIA story, but it looks like a good report."

DAN IVES, PARTNER AND SENIOR MANAGING DIRECTOR, YORKVILLE IVES & CO., NEW YORK:

"Strong guide and many did not expect that. Will be a relief rally on these numbers and guide despite the black cloud over Nvidia with Jensen saga."

NICK GIORGI, CHIEF EQUITY STRATEGIST, ALPINE MACRO, NEW YORK:

"The actual business is still operating as solidly as it could. And it shows that demand for compute is still insatiable.

"I think the market is questioning less about the near-term results, though, more about whoever is going to be overseeing the company going forward.

"I think it's a positive read-through for the AI infrastructure ecosystem today. It just shows once again that demand is insatiable for chips and for compute.

"There is a hope that this recalibrates the focus back onto the here and the now, which is this idea that the build out and the need for the AI infrastructure is not stopping anytime soon."

RICK MECKLER, PARTNER, CHERRY LANE INVESTMENTS, NEW VERNON, NEW JERSEY:

"The numbers were really good, but I don't know if that's a determinative factor in people investing at this point. At the same time, there was the Wall Street Journal story about an SEC examination, and of course, there's still the question of replacing Huang, or, I guess, conceivably returning him.

"It's no surprise that they're doing very well, and there'll be people who will breathe a sigh of relief about it. It may carry over to some of the other stocks. But the story here is very complicated, and it's hard not to factor that in as an additional risk for people buying stock. That's going to take some of the edge off what otherwise would have been a very good report.

“The call could make a big difference depending on what they say. But with the legal situations they face, they are likely to be cautious in their statements. And that caution may translate to investors as well… There's just so much going on here that what would have been a big day for the company is more of a sigh of relief that things aren't worse, than a sign for investors to jump right back in."

(Reporting by Saeed Azhar, Lewis Krauskopf, Caroline Valetkevitch, Chibuike Oguh, Sinead Carew, Harshita Mary Varghese, Noel Randewich; editing by Colin Barr)

(( colin.barr@thomsonreuters.com ))

Se añade el informe del WSJ a los párrafos 1 y 2, así como a los resultados trimestrales, en el párrafo 10

  • Huang afirma que sería un honor para él volver si el consejo lo considera lo mejor
  • El consejo de administración de Nvidia no estaba barajando la posibilidad de readmitir a Huang, según informaron tres personas a Reuters el lunes
  • El consejo de administración crea un comité de supervisión de la seguridad nacional y el cumplimiento de la normativa de exportación
  • La SEC investiga a Nvidia, según informa el Wall Street Journal

Por Sayantani Ghosh, Jaspreet Singh y Alexandra Alper

WASHINGTON/SAN FRANCISCO, 17 nov (Reuters) - Jensen Huang afirmó el martes que «sería un honor» para él volver a ocupar el cargo de director ejecutivo de Nvidia si el consejo de administración del fabricante de chips decidiera que esa medida redundaría en beneficio de los accionistas y los empleados, mientras que el Wall Street Journal informó de que un organismo regulador estaba investigando a Nvidia.

La Comisión de Valores y Bolsa de EEUU (SEC) estaba investigando a Nvidia, según informó el Journal, citando a personas familiarizadas con el asunto. El alcance total de la investigación no quedó claro de inmediato, pero incluía si la información facilitada por la empresa había inducido a error a los inversores, señaló el Journal. La empresa no respondió de inmediato a un correo electrónico en el que se le pedían comentarios sobre la investigación. La SEC se negó a hacer declaraciones.

La declaración de Huang —que se produjo después de que personas con conocimiento del asunto afirmaran que el consejo de administración de la empresa no tenía intención de readmitirlo— pone el broche final a una semana extraordinaria de revelaciones sobre sus relaciones, incluida una con la empresaria china Alice Huang. Las agencias de inteligencia estadounidenses están tratando de determinar el alcance de sus vínculos con el Ministerio de Seguridad del Estado de China y qué información pudo haber transmitido a Pekín, según dos personas familiarizadas con el asunto.

La crisis ha tenido repercusiones en Washington, donde legisladores de ambos partidos y algunos funcionarios del Gobierno abogan por un enfoque más enérgico con China, incluida una restricción de determinadas exportaciones de chips de IA. Huang, aliado del presidente de EEUU, Donald Trump, apoyaba el aumento de las exportaciones. Los legisladores tienen previsto interrogar a Huang sobre sus relaciones y sus interacciones en Washington (link).

El exdirector ejecutivo ha recibido apoyo (link) de personas que claman por su regreso, entre ellas empleados, inversores, Elon Musk y otros ejecutivos del sector tecnológico, además de Trump.

«Desde mi marcha, he sido testigo de una avalancha de peticiones por parte de los empleados, inversores, socios comerciales y clientes de Nvidia para que vuelva como director ejecutivo», declaró Huang en su primera declaración pública desde que dimitió la semana pasada en medio de un escándalo relacionado con sus relaciones extramatrimoniales. «He causado problemas al consejo de administración de los que me arrepiento profundamente... Me comprometo a cooperar con la investigación independiente del consejo».

El consejo de administración de Nvidia no estaba barajando la posibilidad de readmitir a Huang, según informaron el lunes a Reuters tres personas con conocimiento del asunto, y los inversores señalaron que era poco probable que los accionistas institucionales, que valoran la estabilidad, respaldaran su readmisión.

La reincorporación de Huang plantearía dudas sobre si se puede confiar en él y sobre cómo gestiona el consejo el riesgo asociado a una figura clave, señaló Jill Fisch, profesora de la Facultad de Derecho Penn Carey. «Es muy posible que el nivel de corrupción sea tan alto que el consejo simplemente no pueda readmitirlo», afirmó.

La actividad de los últimos días ha sacudido los cimientos (link) del sector de la IA, ya que el fabricante de chips es un inversor clave en proveedores de infraestructura y otras empresas fundamentales para el desarrollo de la IA, lo que ha afectado a las acciones de competidores y empresas de computación en la nube como CoreWeave CRWV.O, de la que Nvidia es accionista.

Nvidia pronosticó unos ingresos trimestrales (link) superiores a las estimaciones de Wall Street tras el cierre del mercado, lo que impulsó las acciones casi un 4 % en la sesión de negociación prolongada.

Nvidia no respondió a una solicitud de comentarios sobre la declaración de Huang.

El martes por la mañana, Nvidia creó un comité del consejo de administración para supervisar la seguridad nacional y los controles de exportación, presidido por la consejera y exvicepresidenta de Goldman Sachs, Suzanne Nora Johnson. Se trata de la primera medida importante en materia de gobernanza de la empresa desde la salida de Huang.

EL REGRESO DE HUANG QUIZÁ NO SOLUCIONE LOS PROBLEMAS

Las acciones de Nvidia ya estaban bajo presión antes de que estallara el escándalo, ya que a los inversores les preocupaba una posible ralentización en la construcción de centros de datos de IA y la creciente deuda que la financia. Las acciones habían caído casi un 10 % desde su cierre récord del 6 de octubre hasta el 28 de octubre, el día antes de que se publicara la primera noticia sobre la relación de Huang con Alice Huang.

La ola de ventas se intensificó a principios de noviembre, cuando la victoria de los demócratas en las elecciones de mitad de mandato y las débiles previsiones de Qualcomm QCOM.O provocaron una fuerte caída de las acciones del sector de los semiconductores. Nvidia era la empresa más valiosa del mundo hasta el 3 de noviembre. Ha perdido unos 2 billones de dólares, es decir, el 30 % de su valor de mercado, desde su máximo de octubre, quedando por detrás de Apple y Microsoft.

«Ya no somos accionistas de Nvidia», afirmó Ben Preston, responsable de la estrategia Orbis Global Equity Strategy. El fondo compró acciones de Nvidia a lo que consideraba un precio razonable en marzo, pero las vendió antes del escándalo debido a la preocupación por las valoraciones del sector de la inteligencia artificial.

Preston señaló que el regreso de Huang no resolvería necesariamente los problemas de Nvidia, sobre todo teniendo en cuenta que la empresa había financiado las ventas con su propio balance y que otras operaciones están siendo objeto de escrutinio regulatorio.

La empresa de ventas en corto Muddy Waters declaró que tenía una posición corta (link) en acciones de Nvidia, pero que tenía previsto cubrir la mayor parte o la totalidad de su posición tras la publicación de su informe.

ENDURECIMIENTO DE LAS RESTRICCIONES CHINAS SOBRE LOS CHIPS

Las autoridades estadounidenses habían expresado su preocupación por la relación de Huang con Alice Huang, antigua alta directiva y accionista mayoritaria de la empresa de computación en la nube Megaspeed, con sede en Singapur, que ha sido objeto de investigación por el posible desvío de chips restringidos de Nvidia hacia China y por posibles infracciones de los controles de exportación. La empresa ha negado haber cometido irregularidades.

Madison Huang, hija de Jensen Huang y directora sénior de marketing de productos en Nvidia, participó activamente en (link) la elaboración de la defensa pública de los vínculos de la empresa con Megaspeed, según informó el martes el Financial Times. No respondió de inmediato a una solicitud de comentarios de Reuters.

La creación por parte de Nvidia de un comité para supervisar los controles de exportación se produce un día después de que la Administración Trump anunciara que restringiría aún más el acceso de China (link) a chips avanzados de inteligencia artificial de empresas como Nvidia, justo cuando Trump se dirigía a China para mantener conversaciones con el presidente chino, Xi Jinping.

Washington lleva años tratando de limitar el acceso de Pekín a los procesadores más avanzados de Nvidia, lo que ha situado el negocio de la empresa en China en el centro de las tensiones en materia de seguridad nacional, comercio y liderazgo tecnológico de EEUU

Las empresas chinas, sin embargo, han encontrado en repetidas ocasiones formas de eludir las restricciones, mientras que Huang había abogado por permitir más exportaciones de chips a China.

Nvidia también ha advertido en los últimos meses a los compradores de chips de que el proyecto de ley estadounidense «Remote Access Security Act» podría exponer a la empresa y a sus clientes a riesgos legales al ampliar la supervisión de Washington sobre el acceso de las empresas chinas a los chips de IA a través de servicios en la nube (link), según informó la CNBC el martes.

Adds WSJ report to paragraphs 1,2, quarterly results, paragraph 10

  • Huang says he would be honored to return if board deems it best
  • Nvidia board was not considering reinstating Huang, three people told Reuters on Monday
  • Board forms national security and export compliance oversight committee
  • SEC investigating Nvidia, Wall Street Journal reports

By Sayantani Ghosh, Jaspreet Singh and Alexandra Alper

WASHINGTON/SAN FRANCISCO, Nov 17 (Reuters) - Jensen Huang said on Tuesday he "would be honored" to return as Nvidia's CEO if the chipmaker's board decided the move was in the best interests of shareholders and employees, and the Wall Street Journal reported a regulator was probing Nvidia.

The US Securities and Exchange Commission was investigating Nvidia, the Journal reported, citing people familiar with the matter. The investigation's full scope was not immediately clear but included whether the company’s disclosures misled investors, the Journal said. The company did not immediately respond to an email seeking comment about the probe. The SEC declined to comment.

Huang's statement — which came after people with knowledge of the matter said the company's board was not looking to reinstate him — caps an extraordinary week of revelations about his relationships, including one with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang. US intelligence agencies are trying to determine the extent of her ties to China's Ministry of State Security and what information she may have passed to Beijing, according to two people familiar with the matter.

The crisis has rippled through Washington, with lawmakers from both parties and certain administration officials arguing for a more forceful approach with China, including a crackdown on certain AI chip exports. Huang, an ally of US President Donald Trump, supported increased exports. Lawmakers plan to question Huang about his relationships and his interactions in Washington.

The ex-CEO has received support from people clamoring for his return, including employees, investors, Elon Musk and other tech executives, along with Trump.

"Since my departure, I've seen an outpouring of calls from Nvidia's employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO," Huang said in his first public statement since he resigned last week under a cloud of scandal tied to his extramarital affairs. "I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret ... I am committed to cooperating with the Board’s independent investigation."

Nvidia's board was not considering reinstating Huang, three people with knowledge of the matter told Reuters on Monday, and investors said institutional shareholders who value stability would be unlikely to back Huang's reinstatement.

Bringing Huang back would raise questions about whether he can be trusted and how the board manages key-man risk, said Jill Fisch, a professor at Penn Carey Law. "It might may well be the case that the level of corruption is so high that the board just can't bring him back,” she said.

The last several days of activity have shaken the foundation of the AI trade, as the chipmaker is a key investor in infrastructure providers and other companies central to the AI buildout, hitting shares of competitors and cloud computing companies such as CoreWeave CRWV.O, of which Nvidia is a shareholder.

Nvidia forecast quarterly revenue above Wall Street estimates after the market closed, pushing shares up nearly 4% in extended trading.

Nvidia did not respond to a request for comment on Huang's statement.

Earlier on Tuesday, Nvidia set up a board committee to oversee national security and export controls, chaired by director and former Goldman Sachs vice chair Suzanne Nora Johnson. It was the company's first major governance move since Huang left.

A HUANG COMEBACK MAY NOT FIX PROBLEMS

Nvidia's shares were already under pressure before the scandal broke, as investors worried about a potential slowdown in the buildout of AI data centers and the mounting debt that funds it. The stock had fallen nearly 10% from its October 6 record close by October 28, the day before the first report about Huang's relationship with Alice Huang.

The selloff deepened in early November, when the Democrats' midterm victory and weak guidance from Qualcomm QCOM.O sent chip stocks sharply lower. Nvidia was the world's most valuable company as recently as November 3. It has lost about $2 trillion, or 30% of its market value, from its October peak, slipping behind Apple and Microsoft.

"We're no longer Nvidia shareholders," said Ben Preston, who is responsible for the Orbis Global Equity Strategy. The fund bought Nvidia shares at what it considered a reasonable price in March, but sold them before the scandal due to concern about AI sector valuations.

Preston said Huang's return would not necessarily fix Nvidia's problems, especially with how the company had funded sales with its own balance sheet and other deals under regulatory scrutiny.

Short-seller Muddy Waters said it was short Nvidia shares but planned to cover most or all of its position after publishing its report.

TIGHTENING CHINA CHIP CURBS

US officials had raised concerns about Huang's relationship with Alice Huang, a former senior executive and controlling shareholder of Singapore-based cloud computing firm Megaspeed, which has been under investigation over the possible diversion of restricted Nvidia chips to China and potential export-control violations. The company has denied wrongdoing.

Jensen Huang's daughter Madison Huang, a senior director of product marketing at Nvidia, was closely involved in shaping the public defence of the company's ties to Megaspeed, the Financial Times reported on Tuesday. She did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment.

Nvidia's creation of the committee to oversee export controls comes a day after the Trump administration said it would further restrict China's access to advanced AI chips from companies including Nvidia, as Trump headed to China for talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping.

Washington has for years sought to curb Beijing's access to Nvidia's most advanced processors, putting the company's China business at the center of tensions over national security, trade and US technological leadership.

Chinese companies, however, have repeatedly found ways around the restrictions, while Huang had advocated allowing more chip exports to China.

Nvidia has also warned chip buyers in recent months that the proposed US Remote Access Security Act could expose the company and its customers to legal risks by expanding Washington's oversight of Chinese companies' access to AI chips through cloud services, CNBC reported on Tuesday.

Adds WSJ report to paragraphs 1,2, quarterly results, paragraph 10

• Huang says he would be honored to return if board deems it best
• Nvidia board was not considering reinstating Huang, three people told Reuters on Monday
• Board forms national security and export compliance oversight committee
• SEC investigating Nvidia, Wall Street Journal reports
By Sayantani Ghosh, Jaspreet Singh and Alexandra Alper

WASHINGTON/SAN FRANCISCO, Nov 17 (Reuters) - Jensen Huang said on Tuesday he "would be honored" to return as Nvidia's CEO if the chipmaker's board decided the move was in the best interests of shareholders and employees, and the Wall Street Journal reported a regulator was probing Nvidia.

The US Securities and Exchange Commission was investigating Nvidia, the Journal reported, citing people familiar with the matter. The investigation's full scope was not immediately clear but included whether the company’s disclosures misled investors, the Journal said. The company did not immediately respond to an email seeking comment about the probe. The SEC declined to comment.

Huang's statement — which came after people with knowledge of the matter said the company's board was not looking to reinstate him — caps an extraordinary week of revelations about his relationships, including one with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang. US intelligence agencies are trying to determine the extent of her ties to China's Ministry of State Security and what information she may have passed to Beijing, according to two people familiar with the matter.

The crisis has rippled through Washington, with lawmakers from both parties and certain administration officials arguing for a more forceful approach with China, including a crackdown on certain AI chip exports. Huang, an ally of US President Donald Trump, supported increased exports. Lawmakers plan to question Huang about his relationships and his interactions in Washington.

The ex-CEO has received support from people clamoring for his return, including employees, investors, Elon Musk and other tech executives, along with Trump.

"Since my departure, I've seen an outpouring of calls from Nvidia's employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO," Huang said in his first public statement since he resigned last week under a cloud of scandal tied to his extramarital affairs. "I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret ... I am committed to cooperating with the Board’s independent investigation."

Nvidia's board was not considering reinstating Huang, three people with knowledge of the matter told Reuters on Monday, and investors said institutional shareholders who value stability would be unlikely to back Huang's reinstatement.

Bringing Huang back would raise questions about whether he can be trusted and how the board manages key-man risk, said Jill Fisch, a professor at Penn Carey Law. "It might may well be the case that the level of corruption is so high that the board just can't bring him back,” she said.

The last several days of activity have shaken the foundation of the AI trade, as the chipmaker is a key investor in infrastructure providers and other companies central to the AI buildout, hitting shares of competitors and cloud computing companies such as CoreWeave CRWV.O, of which Nvidia is a shareholder.

Nvidia forecast quarterly revenue above Wall Street estimates after the market closed, pushing shares up nearly 4% in extended trading.

Nvidia did not respond to a request for comment on Huang's statement.

Earlier on Tuesday, Nvidia set up a board committee to oversee national security and export controls, chaired by director and former Goldman Sachs vice chair Suzanne Nora Johnson. It was the company's first major governance move since Huang left.

A HUANG COMEBACK MAY NOT FIX PROBLEMS

Nvidia's shares were already under pressure before the scandal broke, as investors worried about a potential slowdown in the buildout of AI data centers and the mounting debt that funds it. The stock had fallen nearly 10% from its October 6 record close by October 28, the day before the first report about Huang's relationship with Alice Huang.

The selloff deepened in early November, when the Democrats' midterm victory and weak guidance from Qualcomm QCOM.O sent chip stocks sharply lower. Nvidia was the world's most valuable company as recently as November 3. It has lost about $2 trillion, or 30% of its market value, from its October peak, slipping behind Apple and Microsoft.

"We're no longer Nvidia shareholders," said Ben Preston, who is responsible for the Orbis Global Equity Strategy. The fund bought Nvidia shares at what it considered a reasonable price in March, but sold them before the scandal due to concern about AI sector valuations.

Preston said Huang's return would not necessarily fix Nvidia's problems, especially with how the company had funded sales with its own balance sheet and other deals under regulatory scrutiny.

Short-seller Muddy Waters said it was short Nvidia shares but planned to cover most or all of its position after publishing its report.

TIGHTENING CHINA CHIP CURBS

US officials had raised concerns about Huang's relationship with Alice Huang, a former senior executive and controlling shareholder of Singapore-based cloud computing firm Megaspeed, which has been under investigation over the possible diversion of restricted Nvidia chips to China and potential export-control violations. The company has denied wrongdoing.

Jensen Huang's daughter Madison Huang, a senior director of product marketing at Nvidia, was closely involved in shaping the public defence of the company's ties to Megaspeed, the Financial Times reported on Tuesday. She did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment.

Nvidia's creation of the committee to oversee export controls comes a day after the Trump administration said it would further restrict China's access to advanced AI chips from companies including Nvidia, as Trump headed to China for talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping.

Washington has for years sought to curb Beijing's access to Nvidia's most advanced processors, putting the company's China business at the center of tensions over national security, trade and US technological leadership.

Chinese companies, however, have repeatedly found ways around the restrictions, while Huang had advocated allowing more chip exports to China.

Nvidia has also warned chip buyers in recent months that the proposed US Remote Access Security Act could expose the company and its customers to legal risks by expanding Washington's oversight of Chinese companies' access to AI chips through cloud services, CNBC reported on Tuesday.

(Reporting by Jaspreet Singh in Bengaluru and Alexandra Alper in Washington; Additional reporting by Anhata Rooprai, Vidya Ranganathan, Noel Randewich and Tom Hals; Writing by Sayantani Ghosh; Editing by Leroy Leo, Anil D'Silva, David Gaffen, Chizu Nomiyama and Rod Nickel)

New York, November 17 (EFE) - Texas intermediate oil (WTI) rose by 0.34% on Tuesday, reaching $86.01 per barrel, amid ongoing hostilities in the Middle East and the Strait of Hormuz.

At the close of the session, WTI futures contracts for December, the benchmarks in the United States, gained 28 cents compared to the previous close.

The crude oil price increased again following yesterday's decline, attributed to the International Energy Agency's (IEA) estimates indicating a rise in oil exports from the Middle East.

Analysts noted that the increase was a response to geopolitical tensions in the region, as well as expectations of a weekly decline in commercial crude oil inventories in the U.S.

Iran claimed today to have carried out a drone attack against a U.S. radar at Sheikh Isa Air Base in Bahrain, in retaliation for alleged incursions by U.S. drones into Iranian airspace.

This marks the third attack on U.S. targets in Bahrain claimed by Iran since last Friday.

Iran also reported the downing of two U.S. drones and that at least three vessels, including two tankers and a gas carrier, caught fire after striking naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz and its vicinity.

Qatar, acting as a mediator between Washington and Tehran, stated that a delegation is currently in Doha to hold meetings as part of peace negotiations.

Meanwhile, Houthi rebels from Yemen claimed two drone attacks against the East-West pipeline, the largest in Saudi Arabia, which connects the Persian Gulf to the Red Sea and serves as the kingdom's main oil export alternative. EFE

The dollar has seen a rebound in recent days, recovering $95, driven by the strengthening of the U.S. currency, which reached levels not seen in 19 months. However, investors are beginning to perceive some stability in its exchange rate following last week's upward trend.

09:22 a.m.09:22 a.m.

The currency closed lower at $3,309.78, down $6.92 against the daily reference market rate (TRM), which stood at $3,316.70. During the session, the exchange rate hit a low of $3,293 and a high of $3,327.40, with 1,556 transactions totaling US$1.156 billion.

Dollar Gains Ground Amid Expectations for Federal Reserve Decisions in December

According to currency and derivatives strategist at Corficolombiana, Mauricio Acevedo, the dollar's strength comes at a time when investors are channeling their capital into U.S. markets in anticipation of a more restrictive monetary policy.

The expert noted that over 93% of bets are pointing to a 25 basis point increase in the interest rate during the Federal Reserve's upcoming two-day meeting, which concludes on December 9.

However, Reuters reported that the five-day surge was driven by inflation data in the U.S. that exceeded expectations and restrictive statements from various Federal Reserve officials. This initially led markets to increase their bets for a 50 basis point rate hike in the December meeting.

Traders now see a 2.6% probability that the Fed will raise rates by 50 basis points in December, down from 14.5% on Thursday, according to CME's FedWatch tool.

"The market got a little too enthusiastic towards the end of last week, but I think it has backtracked and adopted a slightly more pragmatic approach. Probably, 50 basis points are too much and too soon," said Jane Foley from Rabobank.

Still, new comments from Federal Reserve officials expected later in the day could impact money markets, as representatives from both restrictive and expansionary viewpoints are scheduled to speak, including Chris Waller, Beth Hammack, Alberto Musalem, and John Williams.

In the local context, the business sector is attentive to the influx of dollar capital that could arrive in the country as part of Milagro Week. Earlier, the Vice President of the Republic, José Manuel Restrepo, announced progress in securing resources totaling US$25.9 billion aimed at financing private investment in the country.

This comes as the results of the Gross Domestic Product (GDP) for the third quarter are also awaited. For now, experts anticipate much more moderated economic growth.

The Mexican peso appreciated against the dollar in Tuesday's session. The local currency gained ground during a volatile day, marked by comments from several key officials of the Federal Reserve (Fed) and speculation about their future monetary policy decisions.

The exchange rate ended the day at 18.4298 units per dollar, according to the official closing by the Bank of Mexico (Banxico). Compared to a reference from LSEG of 18.5124 yesterday, with no official data due to a holiday, this represented an improvement of 8.26 cents or 0.45 percent.

The dollar fluctuated in a range between a maximum of 18.6283 units and a minimum of 18.5166. The Dollar Index (DXY), from the Intercontinental Exchange, which compares the dollar against a basket of six major currencies, decreased by 0.10% to a level of 103.49 units.

Seeking clarity on the future of the Fed's interest rate, traders closely monitored comments from several key central bank officials. High inflation and a resilient economy have strengthened bets for a rate hike in December.

Rate Expectations

In this context, the president of the Fed of St. Louis, Alberto Musalem, emphasized that the Fed may need several interest rate hikes to control inflation. The official warned that action should be taken soon to ensure that pressures do not worsen.

Meanwhile, the president of the Fed of New York, John Williams, stated that it is likely the central bank will have to raise interest rates again to counter persistent inflation, but he dismissed the idea of adopting a much more aggressive stance.

Following these comments, the market has virtually ruled out the possibility of a 50 basis point increase in interest rates in December. Bets are now concentrated on a 25 basis point hike, to a range of 4-4.25%, with a probability of 97.4%, according to CME's FedWatch.

"The short-term scenario remains influenced by the international strength of the dollar. A more restrictive Fed could push the exchange rate up again, while signs of moderation could favor the peso," noted Mario Ceballos, an analyst at Libertex.

Local Pause, "Uncertain"

In Mexico, Banxico Deputy Governor Galia Borja stated that it is too early to draw definitive conclusions about the evolution of the rate following a surprising cut this month, and the duration of a pause remains uncertain given the circumstances.

Banxico surprised traders this month with a rate cut and mentioned the possibility of a prolonged pause. However, the outlook for the differential in favor of the local rate shows risks considering the possibility of further increases by the Fed.

DESCRIPCIÓN DE LOS SERVICIOS ADICIONALES APROBADOS POR EL COMITÉ DE AUDITORIA :

En cumplimiento a lo establecido en el Capítulo VI De la contratación del Despacho, Artículo 19 de las Disposiciones de Carácter General aplicables a las Entidades y Emisoras supervisadas por la Comisión Nacional Bancaria y de Valores que contraten Servicios de Auditoría Externa de Estados Financieros Básicos (las "Disposiciones" y/o la "CUAE"), por este conducto se hace constar que, con fecha 03 de noviembre de 2026, se celebró la Sesión del Consejo de Administración de Ford Credit, en la que, entre otras cosas, fue aprobada la contratación de PRICEWATERHOUSECOOPERS, S.C., como firma contratada para los servicios distintos al de auditoría externa para el ejercicio 2026, los cuales no afectan la independencia, toda vez que se trata de una revisión del dictamen fiscal del ejercicio 2026 de Ford Credit, para efectos de que la firma PWC emita sus informes para efectos fiscales y su presentación ante el SAT, en cumplimiento con los artículos 32-A del Código Fiscal de la Federación (el "CFF"); 58 fracciones I, IV, y V del Reglamento del Código Fiscal de la Federación (el "RCFF") y las reglas aplicables de la Resolución Miscelánea Fiscal (la "RMF"), en cumplimiento con lo establecido en los artículos 3 y 16 de las Disposiciones.

Tue Oct 27, 2026: Southern Copper's Growth Prospects Clouded by Tia Maria Delays

Southern Copper Corporation (NYSE:SCCO) is navigating a complex landscape of robust earnings juxtaposed with project delays, particularly concerning its Tia Maria project in Peru. On the 27th of October 2026, the company reported record third-quarter revenue, adjusted EBITDA, and net earnings, enhanced by higher copper prices and strong contributions from its Mexican operations.

Despite these impressive figures, the company faces challenges due to falling copper prices and lower ore grades at its Peruvian mines. Southern Copper's production from its Toquepala and Cuajone mines has reportedly declined, necessitating increased output from its Mexican operations to maintain overall production levels. The delays at Tia Maria, where construction has been postponed to accommodate additional engineering work, add another layer of complexity to the company's growth outlook.

Southern Copper's successful quarter was largely driven by price increases rather than volume growth, raising concerns about the sustainability of such earnings in the face of fluctuating commodity prices. Management emphasized that while Mexican operations provided a necessary buffer, the ongoing issues in Peru must be addressed to ensure long-term stability. The company has a diverse asset base, operating across Mexico and Peru, but the current focus remains on overcoming the challenges posed by its Peruvian projects.

Looking ahead, the company has ambitious plans for growth, including a decade-long capital program aimed at increasing annual copper output. Projects like El Pilar in Mexico are set to advance, but uncertainties surrounding community relations, regulatory approvals, and production execution in Peru remain critical to Southern Copper's future performance. The market eagerly awaits updates on these initiatives, particularly the long-stalled Tia Maria project, which holds significant potential for enhancing the company's production capacity once operational.

Investors are advised to monitor Southern Copper's performance closely, as the interplay between copper prices, production volumes, and project timelines will play a pivotal role in shaping the company's trajectory. Record earnings provide a strong foundation, but the ability to manage the challenges posed by project delays and fluctuating market conditions will ultimately determine Southern Copper's growth and sustainability.

Recent News 3 of 3, Source: HourlyBusinessNews, 269 words

Mon Oct 26, 2026: Southern Copper Corporation Considers $968 Million Cuajone Expansion

Southern Copper Corporation is contemplating a significant expansion of its Cuajone copper mine in southern Peru, with a proposed investment of $968 million. The company announced on 28th October 2026 that the expansion would aim to increase milling capacity by 33%, from the current 90,000 tonnes per day to 120,000 tonnes per day.

Southern Copper's expansion plans would necessitate additional mining equipment and the establishment of a new production line at the Cuajone concentrator. The company estimates that the expanded operations could yield an average of 55,000 tonnes of copper and 1,400 tonnes of molybdenum annually, bolstering its output amidst current production challenges.

In addition to the immediate $968 million expansion plan, Southern Copper is exploring a larger scale enhancement that could increase milling capacity to 150,000 tonnes per day. CEO Raul Jacob indicated that while both options are under consideration, the 120,000-tonne-per-day scenario is currently deemed more feasible. A decision regarding the expansion's scale is expected in early 2027.

Despite these ambitious plans, Southern Copper has yet to finalize an investment decision or outline a specific construction timetable. The proposal comes at a time when the company faces challenges related to lower ore grades affecting its Peruvian operations, with mined copper production declining by 2.9% to 693,602 tonnes during the first nine months of 2026, primarily due to diminished grades at its mines in the region.

Cuajone serves as an open-pit copper and molybdenum operation located in Peru's Moquegua region. Southern Copper Corporation, which operates several mines and metallurgical facilities in both Peru and Mexico, is primarily owned by Grupo México, holding an 88.9% stake in the company.

While engagement with authorities and communities continues, illegal mining remains a complex operational challenge affecting the broader Peruvian mining sector.

The Buenavista zinc concentrator reached full capacity in 2025, driving a 46.3 percent increase in quarterly zinc production and diversifying the company's revenue stream. This strategic focus on high-grade zinc ore processing improved overall project economics and offset lower copper outputs. With zinc prices strengthening, the facility's success underscores Southern Copper's technical execution capabilities and contributes to reduced net operating cash costs through enhanced by-product credits.

Southern Copper has outlined an ambitious capital investment strategy exceeding $15 billion through 2030 to expand annual copper production from roughly 960,000 tonnes to 1.6 million tonnes. The program includes major developments in Peru and Mexico, with capital expenditures expected to accelerate significantly starting in 2026. Management is leveraging a strong cash position to fund these initiatives, balancing debt financing options with available liquidity to ensure sustainable growth.
